 Purpose of the Commission: The purpose of the HEAR Commission is to advance and
 advocate for equity, access, diversity, social justice, safety, mutual appreciation,
 increased cultural competency, positive inter-group relations and respect for all
 members of the San Gabriel community (the “Purpose”).

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  1. Minutes of the HEAR Commission Regular Meeting on March 22, 2022.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. GUEST SPEAKER- ABDULLAH ZIKRIA, SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA AREA
  MANAGER

  Mr. Zikria, Southern California Area Manager for ICNA Relief, will discuss the
  organization’s efforts with a primary focus on their partnerships with the San

  Recommended Action:

  B. COMMUNITY OUTREACH / PUBLIC INFORMATION PLANNING

  Commissioners will determine ways the Commission can create an outreach
  strategy and plan for the upcoming programs and events that are included
  on the Workplan. Vice Chair Goto to share her findings from a discussion with
  Clara Tsang, Public Information Officer.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends the commission begins developing an outreach strategy
  and determine primary areas of focus for 2022.

  C. DISCUSSION OF APPROVED 2022 ANNUAL WORKPLAN

  Commission members to continue working on the approved 2022 Annual
  Workplan. The Workplan items of primary focus include: Item 1- Equity
  Training, Item 2a- Develop and implement programs and events, Item 2c-
  Guest Speakers and Item 6a- Partnerships.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the HEAR Commission continue working on the 2022
  Annual Workplan.

  D. LAND ACKNOWLEDGMENT STATEMENT

  Land Acknowledgement Statement Advisory Committee members and staff
  to provide an update on progress made toward the development of a
  citywide Land Acknowledgement Statement.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the HEAR Commission receive and file this discussion
  item.

  Each Commissioner may address the HEAR Commission and public on matters

   MINUTES OF TUESDAY, MARCH 22, 2022
  MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS, AND RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Jennings-Nuñez called the regular meeting of the HEAR Commission to order at 6:35 p.m.
on Tuesday, March 22, 2022 with all Commissioners and staff participating by teleconference.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Fitzsimmons.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Michelle Brenhaug, Jacqueline Borja, Susan Fitzsimmons, Viki Goto,
  Jorge Herrera, Riaz (Rick) Khan*, and Chasity Jennings-Nuñez.
  *Riaz (Rick) Khan joined the meeting at 6:37 p.m.

Commissioners Absent:  None.

ANNOUNCMENTS

Recreation Supervisor Matthew Morales-Stevens provided information for the public on how to
submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the HEAR
Commission, e-mail all public comments to mmoralesstevens@sgch.org.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez hearing no objections, the Agenda Order was approved.

  2. PUBLIC COMMENT

  None

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  MARCH 22, 2022
   3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  A motion was made by Commissioner Brenhaug and seconded by Commissioner
  Khan to approve the minutes of the HEAR Commission Regular Meeting for
  February 22, 2022.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 7-0-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Brenhaug, Borja, Fitzsimmons, Goto, Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez, Khan
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. COMMISSION RE-ORGANIZATION

  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Recreation Supervisor, presented this item and
  provided instructions on this process.

  Commissioner Khan nominated Commissioner Chasity Jennings-Nuñez to remain
  as Chair.

  Commissioner Chair Jennings-Nuñez was selected as Chair by acclamation.

  Commissioner Khan nominated Commissioner Jorge Herrera to remain as Vice
  Chair.

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez nominated Commissioner Goto to serve as Vice Chair.

  Adrienne Franquez, Clerk, took the vote for Commissioner Herrera.

  Presented by a vote of 2-5-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Herrera, Khan
  Nays: Brenhaug, Borja, Fitzsimmons, Goto, Jennings-Nuñez,
  Abstain: None

  Adrienne Franquez, Clerk, took the vote for Commissioner Goto.

  Presented by a vote of 5-2-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Brenhaug, Borja, Fitzsimmons, Goto, Jennings-Nuñez,
  Nays: Herrera, Khan
  Abstain: None

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  MARCH 22, 2022
   Commissioner Goto was selected as Vice Chair by a vote of 5-2-0.

  Public Comment: None

  B. REVIEW AND DISCUSSION OF APPROVED 2022 ANNUAL WORKPLAN

  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Recreation Supervisor, presented this item.

  The Commission had the following suggestions:
   Scheduling the social services fair in September to spread out events.
   Proposal of guest speakers, Cheryl Shellhart, StoryCorps organization and
  inviting someone to come in and discuss residents’ rights, citizen rights,
  immigrant rights and provide information to the public on how to run for
  local city office.
   Youth can make a video and hashtag celebrating their culture.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Herrera and seconded by Chair Jennings-
  Nuñez to approve the development of a job fair in 2022.

  Motion denied as presented by a vote of 2-5-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez,
  Nays: Brenhaug, Borja, Fitzsimmons, Goto, Khan
  Abstain: None

  Public Comment: None

  C. LAND ACKNOWLEDGMENT STATEMENT

  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Recreation Supervisor, provided an update on the
  development of the land acknowledgement statement.

  5. COMMISSION REPORTS

  Commissioner Khan shared that April 2nd marks the 1st day of fasting for Ramadan.

  Commissioner Herrera talked about his tour of the city, he visited different
  departments and interacted with city employees.

  Commissioner Fitzsimmons attended the city council meeting held on March 1st.
  One of the guest speakers was Foothill Unity Center, they house and feed people
  who are homeless. They also provide educational training for job seekers.

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  MARCH 22, 2022
   Commissioner Brenhaug shared that it is World Doula week. She also talked about
  the various types of doulas and what they do.

  Vice Chair Goto attended the Southern California Grantmakers panel discussion
  which addresses the urgency of youth mental health. Some of the takeaways were
  that there’s funding available to address youth mental health, importance of
  incorporating the student voice, and to reach students “beyond the couch”. They
  encourage healing through the community. She also wanted to honor Women’s
  History Month, the Women’s March Foundation is hosting a book read of Feminism
  is for Everyone by Bell Hooks on April 5th.

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez shared that she and Vice Chair Goto participated in a
  discussion with Councilmember Denise Menchaca, Mayor Tony Ding and staff
  members of Supervisor Hilda L. Solis. The LA County Board of Supervisors created
  a Blue Ribbon Commission on homelessness to evaluate the current governance
  system of homelessness services administration. They reviewed recommendations
  that are coming in from the Blue Ribbon commission and provided some input.
  She mentioned the San Gabriel Health & Wellness Fair and encouraged the
  commission to attend and meet residents. She also attended a leadership institute
  held at the Duke campus in North Carolina.

  Public Comment: None

  6. STAFF COMMENTS

  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Recreation Supervisor talked about the After School
  Program. The staff have planned activities to celebrate and also educate the
  participants on Lunar New Year and Black History Month.

  Public Comment: None

  7. ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez adjourned the meeting at 8:30 p.m.

  Next regular meeting is tentatively scheduled in person for Tuesday, April 26, 2022 at 6:30
  p.m.
